field_legend.rule_id: K-nn KCC20, M-nn PublicMint, S-nn TokenSeed, numbered in execution (bytecode) order per entry.
field_legend.origin: source = written in the .ag file; argent = added by argentc (visible in .sil); silverc = added by the SilverScript compiler (not visible in .sil); argent+silverc = a builtin call written by argentc and expanded by silverc; engine = the refusal is the engine's own, in an arithmetic opcode of the script
field_legend.sil_line: line(s) of the pinned .sil; "a -> b" = call site -> line inside the helper function
field_legend.bytecode_at: byte offset(s), inside the redeem script, of the opcode that refuses (OpVerify / OpEqualVerify / OpNumEqualVerify / OpReturn; for origin engine the arithmetic opcode). Several values = loop copies or branches. Offsets are the same in every materialized script.
field_legend.op_index: 0-based ordinal of that opcode in the linear disassembly of the redeem script. The engine log (with_opcode_execution_log_buffer) writes one line per PARSED opcode, skipped branches included (crypto/txscript/src/lib.rs:612-613, 656-671), so: op_index = (log lines) - (pushes of the signature script) - 3 - 1 when the last line is the failing opcode.
field_legend.only_via_call_bytes: true = with honest coins, outputs and bindings the rule is decided by the active input's signature script alone
field_legend.needs_raw_bytes: true = only hand-built signature-script bytes reach it; typed call arguments cannot

meta.method: The .ag and .sil files of the pinned reference were read in full. Line numbers are those of these files. Byte offsets and op_index come from a linear disassembly of the pinned bytecode with the opcode table of rusty-kaspa (crypto/txscript/src/opcodes/mod.rs). No source text of the reference is reproduced in this file. Nothing in this file is a result of running an engine.

engine_preconditions.rule: The coin's script public key must have version 0. A higher version is ACCEPTED without running any script.
The signature script may contain push opcodes only (opcode value <= 0x60).
engine_preconditions.note: Checked opcode by opcode while the signature script runs.

engine_preconditions.rule: P2SH check of the coin's own script: the LAST item pushed by the signature script must hash (BLAKE2b-256, unkeyed) to the 32 bytes in the coin's script aa 20 <32> 87. Only then is the stack left by the signature script restored, its top item popped and run as the redeem script.
After the redeem script exactly one item may remain and it must be true.
engine_preconditions.refusal: CleanStack(n) for n extra items; EmptyStack; EvalFalse

engine_preconditions.rule: OpPick reads an item by its depth and is refused at a depth the stack does not have.
Data stack plus alt stack hold at most 244 items.
Script units: one signature check costs the sig-op price and is charged BEFORE key and signature are parsed; an EMPTY signature is not charged (the opcode returns false first).
engine_preconditions.note: The signature rules of the contracts are listed in lists.signature_checks.

engine_preconditions.rule: With covenants enabled the engine demands neither minimal pushes nor minimal numbers: 00, 01 00, 01 80 and 08 00..00 are all the number zero; 4c 04 <tag> is the tag.
engine_preconditions.note: Several byte strings are the same call. A number longer than 8 bytes is NumberTooBig (data_stack.rs:239-251).

engine_preconditions.rule: The signature hash covers no signature script and (transaction version >= 1) no compute commitment. Under type ALL it covers every output: value, script and covenant binding.

The input that runs transfer must be the first input (lowest input index) among all inputs carrying this coin's covenant id.
The number of delegates (the family inputs minus one) is not negative.

rules.meaning: The spent coin's own owner_scheme is one of 0x00..0x04.
Path 0x01 on a coin whose borrow_scheme is 0x00 (disabled) is refused.
Threshold scheme (0x01): nothing may follow the path byte.
Signature scheme (0x02): the bytes after the path byte are a Schnorr signature by the key stored in borrow_guard.
Hash-chain scheme (0x03): exactly 129 bytes follow the path byte (32 next guard + 32 one-time key + 65 signature).
Unkeyed BLAKE3(next_guard || one_time_key) equals the coin's borrow_guard.
Hash-chain scheme: a Schnorr signature by the revealed one-time key.
On the borrow path the spent coin's own borrow_scheme is one of 0x00..0x03.
Borrow path: declared state 0 keeps the leader's owner.
Borrow path: declared state 0 keeps the leader's owner_scheme.
Borrow path: declared state 0 keeps the leader's borrow_scheme.
Borrow path: borrow_guard of declared state 0 equals the expected next guard, byte for byte (the unchanged guard for schemes 0x01 and 0x02; the revealed next guard for 0x03).

Borrow path: declared state 0 amount minus the leader's amount is strictly greater than the threshold (0, or for scheme 0x01 the first 8 guard bytes read as a script number; a negative one counts as 0).
Borrow path: the value (sompi) of the first output bound to the leader is >= the value of the leader's coin.
The path byte is 0x00 or 0x01 (byte comparison: 0x80 is not 0x00).
